original_question: Which neurotoxic protein, produced by Clostridium botulinum, is injected to treat intermittent, involuntary spasms and contractions of the orbicularis oculi muscles (eyelid muscles) in both eyes?

final_qi.question: Which neurotoxic protein, produced by Clostridium botulinum, is injected to treat intermittent, involuntary spasms and contractions of the orbicularis oculi muscles (eyelid muscles) in both eyes?
final_qi.search_keyword: neurotoxic protein Clostridium botulinum treatment orbicularis oculi spasms
final_qi.long_answer: Botulinum toxin type A is a neurotoxic protein produced by Clostridium botulinum that is used to treat conditions involving involuntary spasms of the orbicularis oculi muscles, such as blepharospasm. This toxin works by inhibiting the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, which prevents the muscle from contracting excessively. When injected into the affected muscles, it helps alleviate spasms and achieve a reduction in the involuntary contractions.
